Star chart reads but sits as a flat dark slab; arc lamp pools on the wall, barely on the floor; fridge is the brightest mass and competes with the suit.
Kettle, cups, tiles and bunk with blanket and pillow all read and look cared for; floor in front is grey and empty.

top_issues.issue: Floor is a large dead dark plane that light barely lands on
top_issues.why: The brief asks for lamp and porthole light to pool warmly on the floor; here only the suit's own spot lights it, so half the frame is empty grey-black.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Let the arc lamp, practicals and portholes cast visible warm pools on the floor plating, and add plating detail or a runner so the floor has material.

top_issues.issue: Palettes only recolour the wall band
top_issues.why: Floor, ceiling and fixtures stay identical, so each palette reads as a tint rather than a distinct room.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Carry each palette into the floor tone, trim and practical light colour (and one signature accent per palette) so each one reads as its own mood.

top_issues.issue: Star chart is a flat navy slab
top_issues.why: It reads as a chart only up close; at play scale it is a dark rectangle with no light and no sense of a prized object.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Give the stars and orbit rings a faint glow or a picture light above the frame so it pools on the wall.

top_issues.issue: Fridge out-values the furnishings and the suit
top_issues.why: The large cream box is the brightest object in frame and pulls the eye from the bought items and the suit.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Drop its value a step or put it partly in shadow so the bought pieces and the suit lead.

top_issues.issue: Book shelf and rug feel underfilled at play scale
top_issues.why: Five books and a rug cropped by the frame edge don't make the furnished room clearly richer than stock at the main framing.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Fill the shelf (a row of varied spines, a bookend) and make sure the rug sits fully inside the mid framing.

top_issues.issue: Floor reflections are streaky, slightly smeared, with a teal ghost under the console
top_issues.why: The vertical smears read as a wet or post-process artifact rather than plated metal, and the isolated teal blob reads as a bug; it leans toward realism.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Soften the reflections into broader, lower-contrast pools that follow the plating seams, and damp the console's reflected cyan.

top_issues.issue: Palettes still mostly recolour the walls
top_issues.why: The floor tint helps, but fixtures, ceiling and props are identical, so the palettes read as tints of one room.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Give each palette its own practical light colour and one signature accent (trim material, wainscot, ceiling finish).

top_issues.issue: Star chart is a flat navy slab
top_issues.why: It is a key purchase but has no light of its own and nothing pooling on it.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Faint glow on stars and rings, or a small picture light above the frame.

top_issues.issue: Fridge out-values the furnishings and the suit
top_issues.why: The cream box is still the brightest mass and its reflection adds more weight.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Lower its value or let it sit partly in shadow.

top_issues.issue: Bright reflection directly under the suit lowers its contrast
top_issues.why: The white suit stands on its own bright reflected hotspot, which slightly erodes its edge against the floor.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Keep a slightly darker contact zone under the suit's feet so its silhouette stays crisp.
